data.text:
Davao City: Debt-Free for Eight Years Straight—Yet the Septic Rank Epal Wannabe of the Philippines

Facts first, 2026: Debt-free since 2022 (eight straight years). Assets ~₱37.4B (2024 COA), revenue ₱15.15B in 2025, 2026 budget ₱15.8B. No interest drain funds Bypass tunnels, Samal Bridge pilings, partial BRT—big on paper.

But from an airplane view as an observant visitor would see it in 2026, Davao looks too urbanized spreading horizontally, not vertically: endless low-density sprawl across 2,443 km² (PH’s largest), jeepneys choking dusty diversion roads, mid-rise relics and markets in scattered downtowns, vast rural/empty zones. While others chase vertical density and global polish, Davao doubles down on horizontal mediocrity: low-rise subdivisions exploding, single-story dominance, septic tanks everywhere, flood zones unchanged despite cash.

Septic reality: Mostly individual/communal tanks—no centralized sewer grid. DCWD Septage Plant ~93–100% complete (testing), just for desludging—not pipes. JICA master plan still planning (PMU Nov 2025). Coastal dumps to canals/rivers. “Cleanest” PR while begging for 5-year desludging.

Flooding: 265 prone spots, flash floods hit Damosa/JP Laurel/SPMC/Obrero routinely—clogged drains, garbage, high-tide backups, sprawl erasing buffers. “P9B+ flood control”? Substandard, ghost projects.

COA 2024 roast: ₱8.2–8.7B unreconciled/unreliable PPE—ghost assets, missing inventory, shady figures. Confidential funds ₱530M in 2024 (more than Metro Manila combined).

Epal hypocrisy: Baste’s 2025 anti-epal EO takedown order, but dynasty shadows linger—Duterte brand eternal, performative anti-epal built on one surname.

Debt-free loans, septic-ranked sewers, flooded streets, ghost assets, provincial forever: jeepney chaos, durian banners, no skyline—just horizontal sprawl. BGC/Cebu/Iloilo chase real urban; Davao chases excuses and “no entry” signs. Richest spreadsheets, rankest streets, fakest flex. Septic Rank Epal City in denial. 🔥
📷https://t.co/p1pz1YZHpO

MGA MANGINGISDA NAGPROTESTA

Nagsagawa ng coastal protest ang mga miyembro ng Pambansang Lakas ng Kilusang Mamamalakaya ng Pilipinas sa Manila Bay laban sa serye ng oil price hikes. 

“Sadyang hindi na maawat ang pagsirit ng presyo ng langis. Malaki na ang epekto nito sa mga mangingisda na napipilitan nang magbawas ng oras sa laot dahil sa mahal ng krudo at gasolina.

Samantala, walang sapat na subsidyong ipinamamahagi ang pamahalaan para maibsan ang epekto ng taas-presyo sa aming kabuhayan,” ayon kay Fernando Hicap, PAMALAKAYA National Chairperson. | RH 15 @JecelleRicafort, DZRH News

BREAKING: The MMDA has confirmed that nonstop, or 24/7 repair work will be implemented along Edsa during the Holy Week break or starting at 10 p.m. on Holy Wednesday (April 1) until 5 a.m. on Monday (April 6) or the day after Easter Sunday.

“Yes, we will allow 24/7 work starting Wednesday at 10 p.m. up to Monday 5 a.m.,” MMDA Chair Don Artes says in an interview with INQUIRER.

“Normally traffic is very light on those days. Will issue necessary advisory and deploy personnel to manage traffic flow in construction area,” he adds. | @MJSalcedoINQ
